name: Judea

related_people.name: Archelaus
related_people.role: the harsh ruler of this region whom Joseph avoided, settling in Nazareth instead

related_people.name: Judas
related_people.role: betrayed Jesus to the authorities of this region for thirty pieces of silver

related_people.name: Pilate
related_people.role: Rome's governor of this region, who sentenced Jesus to death

related_people.name: Thomas
related_people.role: urged the disciples to go with Jesus back into this region despite the danger

description: The Roman-era name for the southern portion of the former kingdom of Judah, including Jerusalem, governed at different times by Herod the Great, his son Archelaus, and Roman prefects including Pontius Pilate (Matthew 2:1; Luke 3:1). Jesus's public ministry moved between Judea and Galilee, and it was in Judea's wilderness that John the Baptist preached (Matthew 3:1).
family_friendly_summary: Judea was the name in Jesus's time for the southern part of the land, the area around Jerusalem. It was ruled by kings like Herod and by Roman governors like Pontius Pilate. John the Baptist preached in Judea's wilderness, and Jesus taught both there and in Galilee.
